    "markdown": "## Rule Making Activities

## NYS Register/September 30, 2026

**_Purpose:_** To ensure adequate submetering equipment, consumer protections and energy efficiency protections are in place.

**_Substance of proposed rule:_** The Commission is considering the petition
filed by Archer Ave Holdings LLC (Owner) on June 18, 2026, seeking
authority to submeter electricity to a new rental building with fair-market
and affordable units at 147-27 Archer Avenue, Jamaica, New York located
in the service territory of Consolidated Edison Company of New York,
Inc. (Con Edison). The Commission is also considering the Owner’s
request for a waiver of 16 NYCRR § 96.5(k)(3), which requires an energy
audit for buildings where 20 percent or more of the residents receive
income-based housing assistance.

In the petition, Archer Ave Holdings LLC requests authorization to
take electric service from Con Edison and then distribute and meter
that electricity to its residents. Once approved by the Commission,
submetering of electricity to residential tenants is allowed so long as it
complies with the protections and requirements of the Commission’s
regulations in 16 NYCRR Part 96.

The Owner states that, because the building is new construction
subject to the current New York State Energy Conservation Construction Code, which provides strict energy conservation requirements for
new and renovated buildings, including the design and construction of
energy-efficient building envelopes, mechanical, lighting and power
systems, an energy audit is not necessary.

The full text of the petition and the full record of the proceeding
may be reviewed online at the Department of Public Service web page:
www.dps.ny.gov. The Commission may adopt, reject, or modify, in
whole or in part, the action proposed and may resolve related matters.

**_Text of proposed rule and any required statements and analyses may be
obtained by filing a Document Request Form (F-96) located on our
website http://www.dps.ny.gov/f96dir.htm. For questions, contact:_** Beth
Faranda, Public Service Commission, 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New
York 12223-1350, (518) 474-5306, email: beth.faranda@dps.ny.gov

**_Data, views or arguments may be submitted to:_** Michelle L. Phillips, Secretary, Public Service Commission, 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New
York 12223-1350, (518) 474-6530, email: secretary@dps.ny.gov

**_Public comment will be received until:_** 60 days after publication of this
notice.

**_Regulatory Impact Statement, Regulatory Flexibility Analysis, Rural_**
**_Area Flexibility Analysis and Job Impact Statement_**

Statements and analyses are not submitted with this notice because the
proposed rule is within the definition contained in section 102(2)(a)(ii) of
the State Administrative Procedure Act.

(26-E-0440SP1)

### PROPOSED RULE MAKING NO HEARING(S) SCHEDULED

#### A Process for Offering Flexible Interconnection Service Options I.D. No. PSC-39-26-00026-P

PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE State Administrative Procedure Act, NOTICE is hereby given of the following proposed rule:

**_Proposed Action:_** The Public Service Commission is considering the July
29, 2026, petition by New York State Electric & Gas Corporation and
Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation seeking approval to expand their
flexible interconnection demonstration project.

**_Statutory authority:_** Public Service Law, sections 5, 65 and 66

**_Subject:_** A process for offering flexible interconnection service options.
**_Purpose:_** To provide rules that ensure safe and adequate service at just and
reasonable rates.

**_Substance of proposed rule:_** The Public Service Commission (Commission) is considering the July 29, 2026, petition (Petition) by New York
State Electric & Gas Corporation and Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation (collectively, the Companies) seeking approval of their proposed tariff
amendments to expand the Flexible Interconnection Capacity Solution
(FICS) demonstration project. The Companies indicate that the proposed
tariff language establishes the terms, conditions, and procedures for Flexible Interconnection applications for distributed energy resources (DERs)
to interconnect at Company-identified locations. The Companies explain
that the proposed expansion and tariff amendments are intended to enable
increased utilization of existing distribution capacity by DERs while
maintaining safe and reliable operation of the electric grid.

The full text of the Petition and the full record of the proceeding

may be reviewed online at the Department of Public Service web page:
www.dps.ny.gov. The Commission may adopt, reject or modify, in
whole or in part, the action proposed and may resolve related matters.

**_Text of proposed rule and any required statements and analyses may be
obtained by filing a Document Request Form (F-96) located on our
website http://www.dps.ny.gov/f96dir.htm. For questions, contact:_** Beth
Faranda, Public Service Commission, 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New
York 12223-1350, (518) 474-5306, email: beth.faranda@dps.ny.gov

**_Data, views or arguments may be submitted to:_** Michelle L. Phillips, Secretary, Public Service Commission, 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New
York 12223-1350, (518) 474-6517, email: secretary@dps.ny.gov

**_Public comment will be received until:_** 60 days after publication of this
notice.

**_Regulatory Impact Statement, Regulatory Flexibility Analysis, Rural_**
**_Area Flexibility Analysis and Job Impact Statement_**

Statements and analyses are not submitted with this notice because the
proposed rule is within the definition contained in section 102(2)(a)(ii) of
the State Administrative Procedure Act.
(14-M-0101SP18)

### PROPOSED RULE MAKING NO HEARING(S) SCHEDULED

#### Issuance of Securities and Other Forms of Indebtedness I.D. No. PSC-39-26-00027-P

PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE State Administrative Procedure Act, NOTICE is hereby given of the following proposed rule:

**_Proposed Action:_** The Commission is considering a petition by National
Fuel Gas Distribution Corporation for authority to issue long term debt in
the aggregate principal amount not to exceed $500 million through
December 31, 2029.

**_Statutory authority:_** Public Service Law, section 69

**_Subject:_** Issuance of securities and other forms of indebtedness.

**_Purpose:_** To provide funding for capital needs.

**_Substance of proposed rule:_** The Public Service Commission (Commission) is considering a petition of National Fuel Gas Distribution Corporation (NFG or the Company), filed on September 1, 2026, for authority to
issue long-term securities for permitted purposes under Public Service
Law Section 69.

NFG requests authority to issue up to $500 million of new longterm debt securities at any time through December 31, 2029, for
purposes of (1) reimbursement of the Company’s treasury for money
expended for capital purposes, (2) payment for gross additions to utility plant used and useful in the public service, (3) repayment of shortterm debt obligations outstanding and long-term promissory notes issued by the Company that will mature in 2027 and 2028, and (4) other
corporate purposes.

The full text of the petition and the full record of the proceedings
may be reviewed online at the Department of Public Service web page:
www.dps.ny.gov. The Commission may adopt, reject, or modify, in
whole or in part, the action proposed and may resolve related matters.

**_Text of proposed rule and any required statements and analyses may be
obtained by filing a Document Request Form (F-96) located on our
website http://www.dps.ny.gov/f96dir.htm. For questions, contact:_** Beth
Faranda, Public Service Commission, 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New
York 12223-1350, (518) 474-5306, email: beth.faranda@dps.ny.gov

**_Data, views or arguments may be submitted to:_** Michelle L. Phillips, Secretary, Public Service Commission, 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New
York 12223-1350, ,(518) 474-6530, email: secretary@dps.ny.gov

**_Public comment will be received until:_** 60 days after publication of this
notice.

**_Regulatory Impact Statement, Regulatory Flexibility Analysis, Rural_**
**_Area Flexibility Analysis and Job Impact Statement_**

Statements and analyses are not submitted with this notice because the
proposed rule is within the definition contained in section 102(2)(a)(ii) of
the State Administrative Procedure Act.
